description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with labeled tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, with data recorded at four discrete intervals across this range. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and employs a linear scale ranging from 60 to above 80, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. All six methods display an upward trend across the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circle markers, starting at an ACC of approximately 61.2% at the first data point and steadily increasing to end at approximately 66.8% at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at roughly 62.4% and rising to end at approximately 68.3%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at about 64.5% and increasing to finish at roughly 70.1%. The "MEND" method is indicated by a solid brown line with diamond markers, which starts at approximately 65.8%, rises to 71.3% at the second data point, and ends at roughly 73.9%. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, beginning at about 66.4% and increasing to end at approximately 72.6%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a solid green line with square markers, starting at the highest initial value of approximately 72.3%, rising to 77.6% at the third data point, and ending at roughly 77.7%.
